advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `infra/compose/opcert-ed25519-key` (and `infra/compose/rebar-bot-signing-key`) to .gitignore so the materialized private keys can never be committed.
evidence: fetch-secrets.sh writes the key to `opcert_key_path="$(dirname "${ENV_FILE}")/opcert-ed25519-key"` i.e. infra/compose/opcert-ed25519-key
`.gitignore:88` ignores `infra/compose/.env` but `search_files` for `opcert-ed25519-key` in .gitignore returned `(no matches)`
The precedent `rebar-bot-signing-key` is also absent from .gitignore (`(no matches)`), so this new secret inherits the same exposure
advisory.finding: The materialized op-cert Ed25519 PRIVATE key file (infra/compose/opcert-ed25519-key) is NOT added to .gitignore, unlike infra/compose/.env which is explicitly git-ignored — an operator `git add -A` could commit the passphrase-free private signing key into the repo.
scenarios: Operator runs git add on infra/compose/ after a deploy that materialized the key
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `infra/compose/opcert-ed25519-key` to .gitignore next to the existing `infra/compose/.env` entry (line 88).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that composes a signer from `private_key` (inline PEM) as the sole source and signs a completion/plan-review verdict end-to-end.
evidence: src/rebar/opcert_service/keyprov.py:93-95: `if key_path:` / `return _read_path_source(key_path)` / `return private_key.encode("utf-8")`
tests/unit/test_rp04_s6_opcert_startup_heldout.py:126-131 uses private_key ONLY in the both-set rejection case
ABSENCE: no test composes a signer from private_key alone and drives run_job to a signed envelope
advisory.finding: The inline-PEM key source (`REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY` / `cfg.private_key`) is never tested as a VALID compose-and-sign path. `_read_source_key` returns `private_key.encode('utf-8')` for this branch, but the only test touching `private_key` is `test_compose_rejects_when_both_sources_set` (a rejection case). A regression breaking inline-PEM composition (e.g. wrong encoding, missing trailing-newline handling in `_write_copy`) would go undetected.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a group/other-readable key file (e.g. mode 0644) is rejected by `compose_signer` with `OpcertKeyError`.
evidence: src/rebar/opcert_service/keyprov.py:108-112: `if st.st_mode & 0o077:` raises OpcertKeyError
src/rebar/opcert_service/keyprov.py:40: docstring lists 'too-permissive' as an AC1 rejection case
tests/unit/test_rp04_s6_opcert_startup_heldout.py:72 `_write_ed25519_key` always `key.chmod(0o600)`
ABSENCE: no test writes a 0640/0644 key and asserts OpcertKeyError
advisory.finding: The too-permissive-mode rejection branch in `_read_path_source` (`if st.st_mode & 0o077: raise OpcertKeyError`) is never exercised. It is an explicitly named AC1 case ('too-permissive') in the module/exception docstrings, but every test key is created with `chmod(0o600)`, so a key readable by group/other is never fed to `compose_signer`.
